pairs.why: B's saddle sits over the fence rail in one consistent three-quarter view, with its fenders and stirrup hanging naturally; A shows a flattened, front-facing skirt under a seat seen from a different angle, and its strap drapes across the front.

A's deck planks, posts and hanging lifebuoy all share one clear camera and rest on the posts, while B's tiny pier has posts sticking up through the deck at random and a lifebuoy floating in the middle of the deck.
A's spur is held on by a strap that wraps around the heel counter, while B's star spur shank sticks out from the ankle with no visible way of being attached.

A's yoke clamps onto a truss drawn in perspective, and its lens rim is an ellipse that matches the can's axis; B's tiny truss is seen flat, front-on, while the can below it is tilted, and its light beams fan out without matching the lens.
B hangs flat on the wall and casts a matching shadow, like the real card; A is a round wall clock standing on its rim on the floor with no stand, so it would roll.
A's deck rests on its posts with the lifebuoy hung from a peg, all from one viewpoint; B's lifebuoy floats loose against the deck edge and its rope runs over to a post at an odd height.

In A, the tabletop, pedestal base and stool tops are all seen from the same raised camera; in B the chessboard is seen steeply from above while the stool tops and pedestal are thin, near eye-level ellipses.

A's yoke clamps cleanly onto a diagonal truss, and the lens face, body and side knob share one perspective; B again has a flat, front-facing truss above a tilted can whose beams spread out unconvincingly.
